request.description:
The guard's isProcessCall only matches call expressions whose CALLEE identifier is in PROCESS_ENTRY_POINTS. A test that drives real processes via `execFileAsync = promisify(execFile)` passes execFile as an ARGUMENT (callee is `promisify`) and then calls `execFileAsync(...)` — an identifier the list does not know — so the guard classifies it as not process-driving and demands no bound from it. standin-worker-entry-env.test.ts's three tests (real bash through the real worker entry, declaring 300_000 voluntarily at :105, :116, :132) are therefore entirely unenforced: a future regression of their bounds to a quiet-host number passes every guard assertion. The fixing commit 3cecaa753's own message names the gap ('the guard's static entry-point list does not yet see' the shape). Fix belongs in the guard — recognize the promisify indirection, or add the assignment-target analysis drivenNames already has — and must not over-bind workerd-suite tests that cannot exec.
evidence: harness/test/node/harness-timeout-discipline.test.ts:86-95 (PROCESS_ENTRY_POINTS, isProcessCall); harness/test/node/standin-worker-entry-env.test.ts:29 (promisify(execFile)), :87 (execFileAsync call), :105/:116/:132 (voluntary bounds)

request.title: timeout-discipline guard misses promisify(execFile) as a process entry point
